column1: # Hardware-verified status for instruction-table rows the emu-alltest sweep cannot reach or only reaches
# with a #UD representative (plan 1.15b). Read by Emulator\tools\isa\gen_instruction_table.py; a row
# applies when the sweep alone leaves the row ⬜, or replaces a ⏳ "CPL0 instruction" / "SDM-vector check pending" row
# (U790: the row proves that open item; CPL0 forms keep a Phase 3 CPL3 note); U850: an "sdm" row also applies when the only
# forms the sweep could not compare with the CPU are SDM-pending ones (e.g. WRFSBASE/WRGSBASE, LFS/LGS, which would change the
# host thread's FS/GS natively). Evidence: Emulator\data\cases_reach.txt run with
# status: ok   = implemented, identical to the i5-13600K (✅)
#         sdm  = implemented, the i5-13600K lacks it: verified against SDM-pseudocode vectors (Emulator\data\cases_*.txt "=>" lines, unit tests) (✅)
#         ud   = #UD on the i5-13600K and in Unicorn: correct under the CPU profile, not implemented (⬜)
#         cpl0 = CPL0 instruction, the CPL3 fault differs until Phase 3 (D6) (⏳)
#         oos  = out of scope: not an Intel instruction on this target (⬜)
#         open = implemented, open item named in the note, e.g. a stand-in where the SDM gives only a bound (⏳)
#         spec = implemented, the i5-13600K lacks it: specification-validated against an independent model of the non-SDM
#                Intel document the note names (e.g. ACE 1.15) (✅, always applies; U1094)
#         absent = the i5-13600K lacks the feature; CPU and emulator both execute the absent-feature behaviour (NOP / hint),
#                  the only hardware evidence (✅, always applies; U1094)
#         absent_open = as absent, the feature-enabled semantics have an open item (⏳, always applies; U1094)
#         doc  = implemented, the i5-13600K lacks it: documented compliance - the documents give only an error
#                bound and special cases; checked against an independent model of exactly those (not bit-exact;
# evidence (optional 5th column, U1244): comma-separated evidence labels, SEPARATE from the status (the status
#   stays the architectural / specification evidence); gen_instruction_table.py appends their text to the note:
#   sde-matched       = equal to Intel SDE (labelled reference, not hardware) on every tested input; never
#                       hardware-validated or bit-exact on SDE alone
#   reference-matched = bit-identical to Intel's published reference implementation (article 671685) on every
#                       tested input, and to Intel SDE (not hardware-validated: the i5-13600K has no AVX-512)
#   reference-matched-intel = as reference-matched, against the Intel reference only (Intel SDE does not run the
#                       form, e.g. AVX512ER); the documented SDM-wins / SDM-gap inputs are named in the note (U1248)
